verdict.reasoning: Patient reports headache for "around three days" and confirms it is getting worse: "around three days ago, maybe" and later doctor asks "you think the headache is getting worse over the last three days?" patient: "Yeah."
Onset timing and context are stated: patient says "around three days ago, maybe" and "the first day it just started when I was at work."
Location is described as global with right-sided predominance: "it kind of feels all over my head, but like mainly, um, around my right eye."
Character is described: "it's kind of, it's dull but sometimes it gets a bit sharper."
Severity is explicitly given: doctor asks 1–10 scale and patient replies "Ohh it's probably a eight."

Photopsia/photophobia: "I got this like weird shooting lights. And like now like light is quite annoying" and "Yeah, yeah. It hurts" to look at bright lights. Nausea: patient clarifies "I'm sick with the headache" meaning feels sick. Concentration difficulty: "it's hard to focus though. So, I I had to take a couple of days off work."

No focal neuro/meningitic signs: neck pain/stiffness denied (patient ultimately answers "No." after prompt), speech difficulty denied: "No."; limb weakness denied: "No" to "weakness in your arms and legs"; vision loss denied: "Not loss of vision, I wouldn't say."
Denials are documented: head injury "Uh, no."; fevers "No."; rashes "Mm, no not that I've noticed."
Analgesia trial described: "I tried uh Ibuprofen… I took, like a few. Um for the last two days" and later clarifies dose: "Uh, three a day." and "it doesn't really help, no."
General history: doctor asks "do you have any other medical history?" patient: "Yeah, I think so. It's just the headache." and specifically for migraines: "Not myself, I've never had a migraine."
Medications: "do you take any regular medication?" patient: "Uh, no no." plus recent ibuprofen use described: "I tried uh Ibuprofen… for the last two days."
Allergies: doctor asks "Do you have any allergies to any medications?" patient: "Mm not that I know of." which is equivalent to no known drug allergies.
Family history: "my sister and my mom have them [migraines] quite frequently" and doctor reiterates "you mentioned your mother and sister both have migraines."
Living situation and job: "I live with housemates. So, three of them. So we're four" and "I work in IT. So I work with computers a lot."

Screen brightness change due to light sensitivity: "I work with computers a lot. So it kind of is difficult to focus. Um I had to like reduce the uh, brightness of my screen." in context of photophobia.
Substance use: "I socially smoke. And I drink only socially."

Vision history: "Do you wear glasses?" patient: "Yes, I do." and "I've been wearing them since I was five" and has not had recent test: doctor asks about recent eye test; patient: "No, uh I've been wearing them since I was five…"

Assessment: doctor states "I do think this could be, a headache very similar to a migraine" and discusses migraine-type treatment; absence of red flags is consistent with multiple denials of fever, neck stiffness, neuro deficits, or trauma.
Ibuprofen dosing advice: "You can take up to two tablets, three times a day."
Plan to prescribe naproxen: "I can prescribe you something stronger, like Naproxen…" and later "I can give you a prescription for that today."
Adjunct analgesics: "We can also add in other, painkillers like, Paracetamol, or Codeine. Which might be helpful as well."
Headache diary recommendation: "It may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's… if there's any triggers."

Follow-up timing: "I'd like you to come back and see me, in about uh, a week's time, week to two weeks' time." and earlier: "if your headaches aren't getting any better, or they're getting worse… give me a call, or come back and see me sooner."
Safety-net advice: "if you're having any problems with your vision, or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well. Just give me a call, and come back and see me."

Future prophylaxis discussion: "If you are having more frequent episodes of these type of headaches. We can think about giving you medications as, prophylactic… But we can have that discussion next time."

Optometry consideration: doctor advises "if you feel that you are, your eyes are straining. Um I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done." which is to consider an eye test due to possible eye strain and no recent exam.
